description.narrative: The objective of the COVID-19 (Coronavirus) Emergency Response Project is to prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 (Coronavirus) and strengthen national systems for public health preparedness in Ethiopia. There are five components to the project, the first component being medical supplies and equipment. This component will finance the procurement of medical supplies and equipment needed for activities outlined in the EPRP such as (i) case management; (ii) infection prevention and control; and (iii) other pillars of the strategic plan. The second component is the preparedness, capacity building and training. This component will finance activities related to preparedness, capacity building and training, guided by the different pillars and activities of the EPRP. The third component is the community discussions and information outreach. Activities supported by this component include: risk communication and community engagement; behavioral and sociocultural risk factors assessments; production of RCCE strategy and training documents; production of communication materials; establish a production center for information and communication tools production center (media and community engagement); and monitoring and evidence generation; and human resources for risk communication. The fourth component is the quarantine, isolation and treatment centers establishment. Activities supported by this component include: establishing isolation and treatment centers, including provision of nutrition and dignity kits to quarantined patients, and equipping them with medical supplies and furniture and network installation. Finally, the fifth component is the project implementation and monitoring.
To prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 and strengthen national systems for public health preparedness in Ethiopia.

title.narrative: Number of monthly assessed (using checklist) PoEs, isolation and quarantine centers

comment.narrative:
During the COVID-19 pandemic, a total of 332 isolation centers, 50 quarantine centers, and 64 treatment centers were established and have been continuously monitored using standardized checklists.
* EPHI oversees 12 official PoEs, comprising 8 land crossings, and 4 airports in the country. * To ensure preparedness and effective emergency response, these PoEs and their affiliated nearby health facilities were subjected to regular quarterly assessments, with a focus on referral capacity for passengers presenting urgent medical conditions. In total, 23 sites (12 PoEs and 11 affiliated health facilities) were included in the quarterly assessment framework, resulting in 92 routine assessments annually. * The end target will not be met due to changing priorities from the evolving COVID-19 situation and the temporary PoEs are not currently functional.

title.narrative: Number of airports and PoEs received PPE supplies for airport communities and land crossing PoEs.

comment.narrative: PPE was systematically distributed to all designated PoEs and their nearby health facilities following a comprehensive needs assessment. The assessment incorporated key operational factors including, the average number of incoming passengers, patient volumes requiring medical attention, the influx of returnees and refugees, and the referral and case management capacity of associated facilities to ensure an evidence-based and equitable allocation of supplies.

title.narrative: Achieving the required timeliness of reporting for COVID-19 and other immediately reportable diseases under IDSR

comment.narrative: . This demonstrates substantial progress in early detection and rapid response capacity within the surveillance system. •

title.narrative: Percentage of complaints to the Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) satisfactorily addressed within 15 weeks of initial complaint being recorded

comment.narrative: Following consultations and a clearer understanding of the results indicators, corrections were made to the previous report, and the project status has been adjusted accordingly. To date, the Project has recorded and successfully resolved four (4) grievances within the stipulated 15-week timeframe related to construction and renovation infrastructure works. The grievances were site-specific and addressed through the Environmental and Social (E&S) monitoring framework. To prevent recurrence, the Project has strengthened on-site supervision and oversight mechanisms. A multi-layered monitoring approach, incorporating toll-free hotlines, routine site inspections.

title.narrative: Number of health workers deployed for COVID-19 preparedness and response.

comment.narrative: The factors for the large deployment of health workers during the COVID-19 pandemic include: the intensity and unpredictable nature of the pandemic itself necessitated a massive mobilization of personnel. Furthermore, in many regions, the pandemic coincided with existing or new humanitarian crises, further stretching resources and demanding additional health worker deployments. The rapid implementation of emergency workforce adaptations, such as the redeployment of staff and the recruitment of volunteers and retired professionals, significantly increased the overall number of health workers involved in the response.

title.narrative: Assessment conducted to identify behavioral and socio-cultural risk factors for COVID-19 covering all the regions.

comment.narrative: Research conducted by UNICEF in August 2023 identified several key factors contributing to low COVID-19 vaccination uptake, providing actionable insights to guide targeted interventions. These factors included vaccine hesitancy driven by fear of side effects, misinformation, limited awareness, particularly among adolescents, vaccine fatigue, and shifting health system priorities. Understanding these determinants has informed strategies to improve communication, outreach, and service delivery, to enhance vaccination coverage and address gaps in uptake across different population groups.

Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) developed and implemented: * SOP for Adverse Drug Event Reports and AEFI Receiving and Processing * SOP for Investigation of AEFIs * SOP for Causality Assessment of Adverse Event Reports

title.narrative: Dry storage and cold chain capacity assessed with regards to the COVID-19 vaccines

comment.narrative: During the reporting period, no formal assessment was conducted on the dry storage and cold chain capacity specifically for COVID-19 vaccines. However, the existing national cold chain infrastructure continued to support vaccine storage needs through its established capacity at both central and hub levels. These existing capacities continued to play a critical role in maintaining vaccine potency and ensuring uninterrupted storage and distribution of COVID-19 vaccines alongside routine immunization commodities.

title.narrative: Number of target populations estimated who will be prioritized for access to vaccines stratified by target group (sex-disaggregated)

comment.narrative: During project preparation, the target population for vaccination was limited to frontline workers and older adults with comorbidities. However, over time, national policy changes expanded eligibility to all individuals aged 12 years and above. The total target population estimated for COVID-19 vaccination was 73,918,132 (age 12 years and above). Challenges on effective program planning and implementation include difficulty in obtaining precise target population estimates disaggregated by critical demographic factors specifically, lack of data related to IDP, Refugee, disability etc.

title.narrative: Key COVID19 vaccine messages disseminated through various media outlets (radio, TV, social media, print media etc)

comment.narrative: The COVID-19 vaccination campaign recorded significant overachievement in both awareness and uptake, driven by the implementation of a comprehensive, multi-channel communication strategy. Nationwide dissemination of more than 2.5 million vaccine-related messages was achieved through diverse communication platforms and stakeholder engagement activities. The achieved results were not only with the support of the project but also with the help of key partners, including UNICEF, WHO, SHI 360, Core Group, HEPA, Johns Hopkins University (JHU), and others.

comment.narrative: Vaccination efforts targeting adolescent population groups have been significantly affected by vaccine hesitancy. Analysis of vaccination data reveals a distinct pattern: * Adolescents exhibited a higher degree of vaccine hesitancy compared to other age groups. * Vaccine hesitancy was more prevalent in urban areas than in rural areas. End target will not be met due to shifting priorities resulting from the evolving COVID-19 emergency, and as well as vaccine hesitancy among adolescents.

title.narrative: Percentage of population receiving a booster, which is included in the population targets defined in the national plan

comment.narrative: While the initial rollout of the primary COVID-19 vaccine series was successfully implemented, booster dose coverage remained low, with only 7.77% of the target population receiving the additional dose. Several factors contributed to this limited uptake, including a perceived reduction in risk due to declining severe COVID-19 cases, vaccine fatigue from previous immunization efforts, persistent misinformation leading to confusion and hesitancy, and a reallocation of health system priorities away from booster campaigns.
